findings.location: p. 5 Lemma 3.4 and Notation 3.5; p. 6 Definitions 3.6,3.8 and Notation 3.7; pp. 6–7 Lemma 3.9; p. 10 first paragraph of Lemma 5.4 proof; downstream Proposition 6.1 and p. 13.
findings.claim: Incidence regularity does not imply the many oriented split paths required in Lemma 5.4. The stated configuration conditions admit data with no such long split paths.
findings.admissible_example: Fix eta=1/2, 0<rho<1, small delta>0 and epsilon<1/100 as small as required. Let X tend to infinity, H=sqrt(X), P=H^(epsilon/3), Pprime=H^(epsilon/4), K=PPprime, R=H/K. Take g(n)=1, J={(500Rj,0): X/(10K)<=500Rj<=2X/K}, P1 primes in[P,11P/10], P2 primes in[19P/10,2P]. All scale conditions hold for sufficiently large X for any fixed required C. The grid is strongly separated and has size comparable to X/H; all local sums correlate at phase0.
findings.all_hypotheses: For each p,q, among j in[X/(5000H),X/(1000H)] a fixed positive proportion have dist(jq/p,Z)<=1/100, since q is invertible mod p and the interval contains many complete p-blocks. Put ell=nearest(jq/p); then x=500Rj,y=500Rell belong to J, |y-(q/p)x|<=5R and |x/p-y/q|<=5H/(PK). This supplies >> (X/H)(P/logP)^2 quadruples. All phase differences are0 for every auxiliary prime in[Pprime,2Pprime]; the auxiliary and path prime intervals are disjoint. Each edge has a zero-phase pre-path with positive permitted errors.
findings.decisive_evidence: Any permitted split step has ratio x_next/x >=19/11-10M H/X>=3/2 for sufficiently large X, for the fixed implicit error constant M. Since the entire position interval has ratio20 and (3/2)^8=6561/256>20, no split path of length8 exists. Meanwhile the unfloored expression for k0 tends to3/(2epsilon), so k0+2>7. This rules out even one required path for any modulus, independently of distinct-prime restrictions.
findings.proof_or_calculation: Report Section 2 supplies the full analytic proof. counterexample_check.py independently checks the ratio margin, eight-step growth, scale exponents and exact residue counts for 208 prime pairs. The finite calculation is not represented as checking unspecified asymptotic thresholds. Source pp. 5,6,7,10,11 were actually viewed.
findings.impact: This invalidates the directed path inference used to feed Proposition 6.1 and the proof of Theorems 3.2 and1.1. If regularity means outgoing degree, every nonempty finite subset has a maximal vertex with no outgoing edge, contradicting Lemma 3.9 for these data. If regularity is undirected incidence, it cannot justify Lemma 5.4. This is a Major defect in a core proof chain.
findings.repair_boundary: A suitable stronger selection of prime classes/configuration with a proved directed minimum-degree property, or a different path/counting scheme, is required. Reversing edges changes the fixed split roles used for shared-prime cancellation in Corollary 5.3. The review does not rule out a better selection, disprove existence of configurations in Lemma 3.4, or claim Theorem 1.1 false: g=1 is pretentious.

independent_analytic_reasoning: Definitions and quantifiers: the exact Theorem1.1 range and dependence of C on rho,eta were checked, together with positive errors, torus distance, distinct path primes and coprimality toQ. The closest-root lemma remains valid: in the small-distance regime the multiplication does not wrap; if the permitted error is already large, the root-spacing bound suffices. No additional defect is inferred from the loose introduction notation.

Physical products: on an existing path qi/pi=x_(i+1)/x_i+O(H/X). Expanding a product of length k<=c log(X/H) gives leading telescoping ratio between1/20 and20 and error bounded by(2B)^k H/X; sufficiently smallc controls it. Apply the same argument to the inverted generic path for the lower bound. Products on subpaths then give Corollary4.2 error O(kH/K). Inversion is allowed for a generic path even though it need not remain split.

Pyramid estimates: multiplying the repaired allocated q-edge bound by preceding q products leaves O(K/H), because the prefix ratios q/p are bounded and each remaining prime has sizeP. Telescoping yields4.3 with denominator the initial q product. Applying it also to the inverted subpath and using product comparability gives4.4. These estimates are conditional on existence and do not create long paths.

Counting: distinct prime factorizations give a nonzero reduced rational-product difference at least(2P)^(-2k); k<=log(X/(HB logX))/(2log(2P)) makes this incompatible with O(kH/X) for sufficiently largeB. The cited construction really has500-fold separation and48-fold proximity, so the report correctly does not charge an extra uniqueness defect. For5.2, when q=1 in the cited counting lemma, each integer product has at most r! ordered prime representations; counting integer pairs in the permitted distance gives the asserted absolute constant times A(r!)^2(2P)^r((2P)^r/N+1), uniformly inr.

Shared-prime counting and losses: fixed disjoint P1/P2 roles place a repeated prime on opposite sides of the comparison between two split paths, permitting Corollary5.3 cancellation. The remaining length is2k-1 and multiplicity at most(2k)^2 P/logP. Conditional factorial/logarithmic losses have logarithm O((L/h)logL)+O(epsilon h), where L=logX,h=logH; h^2>=C^2 L logL absorbs them after epsilon is sufficiently small compared withdelta andC sufficiently large. This does not remove the missing directed path input.

Conditional Proposition6.1: two internally distinct and mutually disjoint prime sets make the difference D of the two products nonzero. Corollary4.2 bounds |D| by(kH/X)(2P)^(2k)<=k(2P)^4, hence dy<=H^delta after choosing parameters. The torus relation D alpha_y=O(kK/H) gives a rational multiple ofQy with denominator dividingD plus a small error. Multiplying that error by x0 times the appropriate2k-prime product gives |Ty|<=X^2/H^(2-delta). The position error and kK absorption give the displayed beta approximation.

Global comparison and shortening: the common divisor has logQtilde at least a fixed multiple of c^k Pprime, which dominates logX under the stated H threshold. A nonzero rational multiple ofQtilde with denominator bounded byH^(2delta) is too large for the available Ty/T error, forcing the exact rational congruence and |T-Ty|<=x0 H^(delta-1). Pigeonholing dy and the common-divisor selection retain the stated X/H^(1+3delta) scale. H*=H^(1-3delta)<=H/K; triangle inequality over shorter blocks provides one correlated block, and |T/y-T/z|<=K H^(delta-1)<=H^(2delta-1) makes its phase error negligible for delta sufficiently small relative torho. Projection modulo1 uses the integer modulus. The final two sums on p13 need absolute values, as the initial report already records.
